title: First-Notice Extension of a Home-Site Lease Cure Period — Training Cases
content:
**Training note: earlier nonpayment notices and the cure period**

The cure period of a nonpayment notice on a Home-Site Lease is lengthened by a first-notice extension, in days, read from the nonpayment notices already served on the lease.

**Rule.** The extension is 3 days when no nonpayment notice was served on the lease in the trailing twenty-four calendar months; 1 day when one or more was served in that window but none in the trailing twelve calendar months; and none otherwise, that is, when a nonpayment notice was served in the trailing twelve calendar months.

| Nonpayment notices served on the lease | Extension |
|---|---|
| none in the trailing 24 calendar months | 3 days |
| one or more in the trailing 24 calendar months, none in the trailing 12 | 1 day |
| one or more in the trailing 12 calendar months | none |

### Cases (notice to be served on 4 May 2026)

1. *The lease has never had a nonpayment notice* — 3 days.
2. *The only earlier notice was served in January 2024* — more than 24 months before: 3 days.
3. *The only earlier notice was served in October 2024* — inside 24 months, outside 12: 1 day.
4. *An earlier notice was served in December 2025* — inside 12 months: none.
5. *Notices in October 2024 and December 2025* — one inside 12 months: none.
